topics.topic: Atomic validation and delivery of multiple mapped outputs when one is oversized
questions: If one delivered mapped output exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, are all outputs of that mapped node withheld atomically, or can other valid output ports still be delivered or appear as run outputs; and in what order are several delivered outputs measured?
Are all mapped output lists validated atomically before any is delivered, or may earlier valid outputs remain delivered when a later output is oversized?

When a mapped node has several used outputs and one derived list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, are all used outputs checked atomically before any delivery, or can smaller outputs already reach other branches?

quotes:
a mapped node's value list above it fails the node for
   its dependants without changing any element's record (A13 rule 6);

Only a list that is
   delivered — to a node or a flow output — is measured; an output no edge
   takes fails nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates all used mapped outputs atomically and withholds every output if one is oversized; another delivers smaller outputs before discovering the oversized output. Downstream nodes, external services, and callers reading run outputs notice the difference.
judgement.why: The new mapped-list rules define the oversized list's failure but not cross-output atomicity or measurement order.

precedent.topic: Reliable detection of sandbox resource-limit exhaustion
quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the parent's setrlimit, set above process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside: the environment was killed for it, or a MemoryError, or an OSError for a full or over-limit exchange directory, escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned, like any other output (owner, 2026-10-06). Only the process bound is also seen inside, because every thread start and os.fork passes the runner's audit hook.

execute_function: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the wall deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the channel recorded any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the module failed to load, has no run, raised, or the process exited abnormally; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, a value output cannot be serialized to canonical JSON, a file output is not bytes, a many output is not a list, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value ceiling and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's: the module that stores or spools an output applies them after the execution has otherwise succeeded.
precedent.why: The later sandbox contract defines parent-visible resource evidence, special process-limit reporting, caught-error behavior and the precedence against `crashed`.

topics.topic: Symlink-safe, race-free resolution of configuration and credential paths
questions: Are symbolic links forbidden only at the final path component, or in every ancestor component of the absolute configuration and secret paths, and how are path-replacement races handled?
How must the kernel prevent a path replacement between validation and reading the credential?
May any parent component of a configuration or secret-file path be a symbolic link?

quotes:
The file
   must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, owned by the kernel's user, with
   no permission for group or others; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.

A credential is resolved only when a request to its service is built: its
   secret file is read then, without following a symbolic link, and must be a
   regular file owned by the kernel's user with no permission for group or
   others; its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the
   value.
judgement.divergence: One implementation rejects symlinks in every path component and validates the opened file descriptor; another rejects only a final-component symlink and separately checks then reopens the path. The installer and service observe different acceptance or credential use, and an attacker can observe whether path replacement succeeds.
judgement.why: The filesystem rules do not define ancestor-link handling or require validation and reading to use the same opened file object.

precedent.topic: Retry behavior for an unchanged invalid configuration
quotes: current_token_list: [BEHAVIOR] On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes and compare their SHA-256 with the last read digest; when equal it returns the kept list unchanged (none stays none); when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file and applies exactly four checks: the file can be read and parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types, every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long, no two tokens are equal, and no two agent tokens have the same name; the new digest becomes the last read digest, and when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared, so the next readable bytes are always re-read.

current_token_list: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] When all four checks hold, the re-read's tokens replace the kept list; when any fails the kept list becomes none and the old list is discarded, since it may hold a revoked token; a re-read takes only the token list, and no other field of the kept Installation changes until a restart.
precedent.why: The later contract says invalid readable bytes become the last-read digest, so unchanged invalid bytes are not reparsed and the retained token list remains none.

topics.topic: Validity of existing admissions after a sandbox-runtime upgrade
questions: After installing a new release, may previously admitted implementations and unfinished runs execute under the new sandbox runtime without re-admission, even if their outputs or trap behavior can change?
Does an admission verdict remain valid after upgrading to a release with a different sandbox runtime?

judgement.why: This is the same question about reuse of admission verdicts across release upgrades.

precedent.topic: Validity and reuse of admission verdicts across executions and release upgrades
quotes:
Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
   admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
   current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.
precedent.why: Whether cached verdicts and pinned implementations survive a release change was already unspecified around this unchanged reuse rule, and the change did not make that question newly material.

topics.topic: Whether authentication tokens require valid base64url encoding
questions: Must a token be valid unpadded base64url decoding to at least 32 bytes, or is any string of at least 43 characters accepted?
Must a token be valid base64url encoding of at least 32 bytes, or is any string of 43 characters accepted?

quotes: read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not a regular file or is a symbolic link (checked without following links), is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name.
judgement.why: The later installation contract lists token length, equality, and name uniqueness as the token checks and imposes no base64url decoding requirement.

topics.topic: Whether operation outputs may have a lower disclosure class than their inputs
questions: May an operation output have a lower disclosure class than the inputs supplied to that operation?
May an operation node emit a value whose declared output class is lower than one or more of its actual input classes, or must its output be raised to at least the highest input class?

quotes:
At proof time the class that can reach a node's output is: for an operation
   node, the class its binding declares for that output; for a function node, the
   highest class that can reach any of its inputs, `open` when it has none; for a
   flow input, the class its port declares; for a constant, the class the
   composing agent declared with it.
No function, edge or flow construct lowers a class.
judgement.why: An operation node is assigned its binding-declared output class regardless of a higher input class, while the same decision says no flow construct lowers a class.
